input.question: Why the hell does my cable box/ DVR take forever to change channels? Why does it make me wait no matter what I ask it to do?
input.ground_truth: On some, the tuner going to another channel is slow because of the remote. In order to avoid false changes, the remote codes for each digit are transmitted very, very slowly. My old Gen1 Tivo had the ability to set the remote codes to be fast/medium/slow for this reason, since it was relying on an "IR blaster" to tell the cable box to change the channel. It was a crappy design and was prone to changing to the wrong channel if there was bright sunlight in the area. In general, most cable boxes and DVRs can change channel quite rapidly once they get the code from the remote. My new Tivo does.

Question: Why the hell does my cable box/ DVR take forever to change channels? Why does it make me wait no matter what I ask it to do?

response.prediction:
Okay, let's imagine your cable box is like a little robot that lives inside your TV.

When you want to watch a different channel, you tell the robot, "Hey, show me cartoons!" But the robot is a little slow. It has to stop what it's doing, look for the cartoons, and then bring them to your TV.

It takes time because the robot has to check a lot of things—like where the cartoons are stored, if it needs to ask the big computer far away for help, and then it has to get everything ready just right before it can show you the cartoons.

So even if you tell it really fast or really loud, the robot just needs a little while to do all its steps. That's why you have to wait, no matter what you ask it to do. It's not being naughty—it's just a little slow, like when you try to put on your shoes but it takes a few tries to get them on the right feet!
